disclaimer: This is a reference tool, not an inspection. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or connected to the United States Coast Guard or the Coast Guard Auxiliary. It covers federal carriage requirements only; your state may require more.

base.title: Life jackets
base.detail: One Coast Guard approved wearable life jacket for each person aboard, 4 needed. Each must be serviceable, the right size for its wearer, legibly marked with its approval number, and readily accessible, not locked away or buried under gear. A life jacket whose label sets conditions, such as a Type V that must be worn, counts only when used the way its label says. Inflatables are approved only for the ages printed on them.

base.title: Children under 13
base.detail: If a child under 13 is aboard while underway, the child must wear a Coast Guard approved life jacket unless below decks or in an enclosed cabin. Where your state sets its own age for children, the state rule applies instead on its waters.

base.title: Visual distress signals
base.detail: Not federally required on inland waters. Required on coastal waters: the Great Lakes, the territorial seas, and waters connected to them out to the first point where the shores narrow to 2 nautical miles apart.

base.title: Sound signals
base.detail: Some means of making an efficient sound signal, such as a horn or a whistle loud enough to be heard. Under 12 m (39.4 ft) the full-size whistle is not required.

base.title: State and local requirements
base.detail: Your state may require more than this list: a fire extinguisher where federal rules do not, a different age for children's life jackets, registration of a boat with no engine, or a boating safety certificate. This app covers FEDERAL carriage requirements only.

added.title: Navigation lights
added.detail:
From sunset to sunrise and in restricted visibility.
• A paddled or rowed boat may show the sailing lights (sidelights and a sternlight)

added.title: Visual distress signals
added.detail: Night signals only, carried between sunset and sunrise: 1 electric distress light, or 3 approved red flares (hand-held or aerial). No day signals are required for this boat. Readily accessible, marked with the approval number, and within the date on them.

base.title: Registration and numbering
base.detail: A boat with propulsion machinery of any type, an electric motor included, must be numbered by your state. Carry the certificate of number aboard, on paper or in digital form. Display the number on each side of the forward half in plain vertical block characters at least 3 inches high, in a contrasting colour, with the validation sticker beside it as your state directs. A Coast Guard documented boat is not state numbered under this rule.

base.title: Anchor ball
base.carry: One black ball, if you anchor by day
base.detail:
At anchor by day, show one black ball forward where it can best be seen.
Not required under 7 m (23 ft) away from channels, fairways, anchorages and where other boats normally navigate, or in a Coast Guard special anchorage area.
Under 20 m a ball smaller than the full 0.6 m size is allowed, in keeping with the size of the boat.
It is a daytime rule, so it applies even if you never go out after dark. At night the anchor light takes its place.

added.title: Navigation lights
added.detail:
From sunset to sunrise and in restricted visibility.
Underway, a power-driven boat shows:

variants.label: Has a closed space where fuel vapour can collect, or a permanent fuel tank

added.title: Fire extinguishers
added.detail:
Carry 1 x 5-B portable extinguisher. Required on this small outboard boat because it has a space where fuel vapour can collect.
Each one must be:
• On board and readily accessible, and an approved type
• Not expired, and not used
• Gauge in the operable range, pin in place, nozzle clear
• Free of significant corrosion or damage
Model year 2018 and newer: 5-B or 20-B rated units with a date stamp. Model year 2017 and older may keep serviceable B-I (counts as 5-B) or B-II (counts as 20-B) units.
The Coast Guard treats a disposable extinguisher as expired 12 years after the manufacture date stamped on it.

added.title: Ventilation
added.carry: Vents if a gas tank is built in
added.detail: For a gasoline outboard: a closed compartment holding a permanently installed gasoline tank needs natural ventilation (cowls and ducts to the lower part of the space) unless it is open to the air. A portable tank in a seat locker does not by itself call for it.

added.title: Ventilation
added.detail: Each compartment with a permanently installed gasoline engine must be open to the air or have an exhaust blower, with the label near the ignition switch: run the blower for 4 minutes before starting. A compartment with a permanently installed fuel tank needs natural ventilation (cowls and ducts) unless it is open. Boats built after 31 July 1980 must keep the system the builder fitted working; older boats need two ducts with cowls to each engine and tank space.

added.title: Backfire flame control
added.carry: Flame arrestor on each gas engine
added.detail: Every gasoline engine installed after 25 April 1940, except outboards, needs an acceptable means of backfire flame control, usually a flame arrestor on the carburetor or throttle body. Look for a Coast Guard approval number (162.015, 162.041 or 162.042), or an SAE J-1928 or UL 1111 marking. Keep it clean and secured.

variants.label: Has an installed toilet

added.title: Marine sanitation device
added.detail: An installed toilet needs an operable, certified marine sanitation device: Type II or III, or Type I at this length. In a No Discharge Area, secure it so nothing can go overboard, for example seacock closed with the handle removed, or padlocked or wire-tied shut.
